To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
FcgammaR IIa R131, IIa F176, and IIb NA2 polymorphisms are genetic factors associated with susceptibility to AOSD.

polymorphisms of the FcgammaR were not associated with development or course of AOSDs in Korea, but the haplotype II R131-II F176-II NA2 was more frequently observed in AOSDs than in healthy controls.
the haplotype Fc gamma RIIA R131-IIIAF176-IIIBNA2 was more frequent and Fcgamma RIIA R/R131 and H/R131 genotype were more frequent in Korean AOSD patient than in healthy controls.

the association of FcgammaRIIIA polymorphism with AOSD in Korean patients.
the association between FcgammaR gene polymorphisms and the development or course of AOS D in Korea.
the association of FcgammaRII polymorphisms in patients with AOD.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
these polymorphisms of the FcgammaR are not associated with the development of AOSDs in Koreans.
the Fcgamma receptor gene polymorphism is a risk factor for the chronic articular-type of AOSD, but not for AOSD in general.
FcgammaR may be associated with the chronic articular type and the FcgammaR haplotype with AOSD in Korean patients.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FcgammaR may not be associated with susceptibility to AOSD in Korean population, but it may influence disease severity or disease course.

the polymorphisms in the Fc-gamma receptors are not associated with the susceptibility of adult onset Still’s disease, but they might be associated with the disease course of the patients with adult onset Still’s diseases in Korean population.

the FcgammaR IIA, IIIA, and IIIB polymorphisms were not significantly associated with AOSDs in Koreans; however, the FcgammR IIA R/R131 genotype and the IIA R131/IIIA F176/IIIB NA2 haplotype were significantly associated with the chronic articular type of AOSD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the FcgammaR IIa R131, IIIa F176, and IIb NA2 haplotype was associated with AOSd in Koreans.
FcgammaRIIa polymorphism is not associated with development AOSD in Korean patients.

the Fc gamma receptor polymorphisms are likely to be associated with AODS in Korean patients, and the haplotype of the Fc gamma R polymorphisms may be associated with the chronic articular type of AODS.
